summary: Use a Tab Item inside Tabs for each view: a short label that turns black with a gold underline while its view is showing.

useWhen.text: Use a Tab Item inside Tabs for each view: a short label that turns black with a gold underline while its view is showing.

avoidWhen.text: On its own, outside Tabs: a lone Tab Item stretches across its container with no row around it. Use it inside Tabs.

from.quote: A lone Tab Item stretches across its container with no row around it.

avoidWhen.text: The tab would do something, such as “Download”: it sounds like a button, but tabs only switch views.

from.quote: “Download” sounds like a button, but tabs only switch views.

from.quote: There is no disabled state.

placementAdvice.text: Always place a Tab Item inside Tabs.

from.quote: One view, one short label, and always inside Tabs.

placementAdvice.text: Tabs places the tabs 16 px apart; a Tab Item is as wide as its label.

from.quote: It is as wide as its label; Tabs places the tabs 16 px apart.

configuration.text: Set label to name the view; the label is also what screen readers say.

from.quote: The label is also what screen readers say.

configuration.text: Set badge when a view needs a count: it shows the counter badge from Figma.

from.quote: when a view needs a count, the counter badge from Figma

configuration.text: Set active on the tab whose view is showing: the screen marks it, and a Tab Item never selects itself.

from.quote: The screen marks the tab whose view is showing as active; a Tab Item never selects itself.

configuration.text: Mark one tab active: one underline shows the current view.

from.quote: One underline shows the current view.

configuration.text: Do not mark two tabs active: only the first is underlined, which may not be the view that’s showing.

from.quote: Only the first is underlined, which may not be the view that’s showing.

configuration.text: Handle onPress on each tab: the screen marks one active and swaps the panel when another is pressed.

from.quote: The screen marks one active and swaps the panel when another is pressed

rules.text: Name the view in one or two words.

from.quote: One or two words that name the view

rules.text: Write a noun in sentence case, such as “Statements”.

from.quote: Write a noun in sentence case, such as “Statements”.

rules.text: Don’t write actions like “Download” or long phrases.

from.quote: Don’t write actions like “Download” or long phrases

states.when: active is false (the default): grey label, no underline.

from.quote: Grey label, no underline.

states.when: active is true, set by the screen for the view that is showing: black label and a gold underline across the tab.

from.quote: Black label and a gold underline across the tab.

states.when: While pressed: the tab dims to 70% until release.

from.quote: Pressing dims it to 70% until release.

accessibility.text: Give an abbreviated label a full spoken name with accessibilityLabel, such as AY24 as “Assessment year 2024”.

from.quote: Short labels such as AY24 get a full spoken name: “Assessment year 2024”.

accessibility.text: On the web a tab is announced by its label or spoken name and whether it is selected.

from.quote: On the web a tab is announced by its label or spoken name and whether it is selected.

accessibility.text: Only the selected tab is in the Tab order, or the first one when none is selected, and a Tab Item on its own is always reachable; Enter and Space select a tab, and the arrow keys move between tabs.

from.quote: Only the selected tab is in the Tab order, or the first one when none is selected, and a Tab Item on its own is always reachable; Enter and Space select a tab, and the arrow keys move between tabs.

examples.purpose: Tax years over one panel: abbreviated labels, each with a spoken name, and the showing year marked active.
examples.jsx:
<Tabs modes={{ 'Color Mode': 'Light' }}>
  <TabItem label="AY24" accessibilityLabel="Assessment year 2024" onPress={() => {}} />
  <TabItem label="AY25" accessibilityLabel="Assessment year 2025" active onPress={() => {}} />
  <TabItem label="AY26" accessibilityLabel="Assessment year 2026" onPress={() => {}} />
</Tabs>

props.name: label
props.description: Label text to display. Default "Tab item", from the component source.

props.name: active
props.description: Set by the screen; a Tab Item never selects itself. In a row with two active items, the second is ignored: only the first is selected. Declared: Whether this tab item is currently active/selected. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Enter and Space each call it once (#209 fixed). Declared: Callback when this tab item is pressed.

props.name: modes
props.description: Inside Tabs, a Tab Item receives the row's modes; its own modes win. Declared: Design token modes for theming.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Becomes the tab's accessible name on the web; without it, the label names the tab. Declared: Accessibility label for screen readers.

props.name: badge
props.description: Shows a CounterBadge beside the label. Declared: Optional counter shown beside the label. Matches the Figma tab badge.

props.name: testID
props.description: Works since the 636f3f5 build (the 5 October check found none). Declared: Test identifier.

props.name: truncateLabel
props.description: Set by Tabs on a non-scrollable row so a long label ellipsizes instead of pushing the last tab outside the row. Standalone items keep hugging. Default false, from the component source.

props.name: isTabStop
props.description: Set by Tabs. When omitted, a standalone item stays in the tab order. Inside a row, only the active tab (or the first tab when none is active) is true.

modes.name: Color Mode
modes.description: A token collection TabItem reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

events.name: onPress
events.description: Callback when this tab item is pressed

gaps.text: The active label stays black in Dark mode (#197, To do); the guide shows Light only.
